name: ref_2
description: Print of a 4-board 3x3 ChArUco sheet, serial ref_2.

_provenance.measured: NOT YET TAKEN. Six caliper readings on each printed span, outer edge to outer edge, WHILE THE SHEET IS STILL INTACT -- after cutting the longest baseline inside one piece is too short to see the print error. See docs/planning/measuring-the-printed-target.md.
_provenance.printer: Record the make and the driver's scaling setting. ref 1 came out 4.75 per cent undersize because 'fit to printable area' was left on.
_provenance.scale: 4.70 per cent undersize, uniform 0.95303 from 6 readings per axis in ONE sitting. ref_1 came out 0.95251, so the two prints agree to 0.052 per cent: this printer's 'fit to printable area' is highly reproducible, and ref_2 was made from artwork that predates the PRINT AT 100 % instruction. ref_3 should be printed with scaling off.
_provenance.anisotropy: +0.019 per cent +- 0.058, 0.3 sigma -- not detected, agreeing with ref_1's +0.057 +- 0.100. Two prints now say this printer has no measurable anisotropy.
_provenance.shear_detected: UNRESOLVED and recorded as null rather than true. The diagonals differ by -0.390 mm against a 2 sigma floor of 0.318, which is 2.45 sigma, but n is 3 and the whole result rests on one low reading of 144.28 against 144.66 and 144.79. That is the shape of the artefact that produced and then destroyed ref_1's +0.273 per cent anisotropy. If real it is 0.154 degrees, which inside one 48.6 mm cut piece is 0.130 mm, 16 per cent of the error budget. Tranche 2 settles it.
_provenance.diagonals: DO NOT USE FOR SCALE. They give 0.94802 where the axes give 0.95303, reading 0.501 per cent short -- ref_1 read 0.345 per cent short the same way. At 144.9 mm the jaws are at 95 per cent of travel and splay. Their scatter is also the worst on the sheet, 0.265 mm against 0.006 to 0.191 on the axes.
_provenance.uniformity: No drift detected. Rows differ by +0.113 mm +- 0.111 (1.03 sigma) and columns by -0.053 +- 0.039 (1.35), both inside noise.
_provenance.readings_mm: across #0-#1 came in at sd 0.006 mm -- three readings inside one caliper count. That is not three independent seatings; compare sd 0.191 on the nominally identical #2-#3 span. Release the jaws fully between readings.

readings_mm._what_was_seated_on: outer edges of the black squares, board to board
readings_mm._tranches: Tranche 1 only. The protocol asks for 3 readings in one sitting and 3 in another on each span, because ref 1's down span moved 0.707 mm between sittings, thirteen times the scatter within one. Everything derived below is provisional until tranche 2.
